title: The I3322 quantum value is attained spatially but not in finite dimension
description: Three theorems about the I3322 Bell functional, working from an exactly certified window for its quantum value S and a certified tensor/commuting value equality. Theorem (N): no finite-dimensional quantum strategy attains S (any local dimensions, mixed states, POVMs), proving the 2010 conjecture of Pal and Vertesi. Theorem (S): S is attained by a spatial strategy on l2(Z) tensor l2(Z). Consequently C_q(3,3;2,2) is not closed and C_qs \ C_q is nonempty, at the smallest venue by input count, among two-outcome bipartite scenarios, in which nonclosure is known; no minimality is claimed over larger output alphabets. Theorem (Rate): the dimension complexity is D(eps) = Theta(log(1/eps)) - reaching S to accuracy eps requires and suffices local dimension of order log(1/eps), with explicit derived constant 23.9010650 on the upper half and existential constants on the lower. The exact optimum beyond the certified 3.61e-9 window, and whether the Pal-Vertesi family converges to S, remain open. The repository ships the paper (paper/resolution.pdf), machine-checkable certificates with complete audit records, a Lean 4 kernel (27 theorems, standard axioms only), and the full correction history, including the public decertification of an earlier claimed proof by this program.
